node.title: Re: Generating Message_id email headers
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I would strongly recommend you look into getting the module installed, either locally into your account, or perhaps even by your hosting provider. See [id://693828] and [mod://local::lib]. It's a pure-Perl module consisting of a single file, so in the worst case you could even just copy the file over.

And in the very worst case, note that the guts of the module [mod://Email::MessageID] are actually quite short. Although as I said I strongly suggest getting it installed, if you really have no choice, here is a boiled-down version:

# Code derived from Email::MessageID 1.406 by Ricardo Signes # http://cpansearch.perl.org/src/RJBS/Email-MessageID-1.406/lib/Email/MessageID.pm use Sys::Hostname::Long qw/hostname_long/; my @CHARS = ('A'..'F','a'..'f',0..9); my %uniq; sub create_mid { my $noise = join '', map {; $CHARS[rand @CHARS] } (0 .. (3 + int rand 6)); my $t = time; my $u = exists $uniq{$t} ? ++$uniq{$t} : (%uniq = ($t => 0))[1]; my $user = join '.', $t . $u, $noise, $$; return '<' . $user . '@' . hostname_long . '>'; }

You can replace hostname_long with hostname from [doc://Sys::Hostname] if you don't have [mod://Sys::Hostname::Long] installed.
